user_input: Everyone in my hostel wing has these tight-knit regional groups, and they all speak their home language. When I walk into the mess, they're laughing and sharing food, but the moment I sit down, the conversation just dies down or they switch to English out of pity. I ended up wrapping my dinner in a roti today and eating it in my dark room while doing a DSA lab. I’ve been here six months and I still feel like a complete intruder in my own college.

We had to form groups of four for the DBMS capstone project today. The professor said 'find your partners' and the entire lecture hall just erupted into chaos, people grabbing their friends, and I just sat there pretending to look busy on my GitHub profile. I was the last one left, and the prof had to awkwardly assign me to a group that already had three people who clearly didn't want me there. My CGPA is 9.1, I'm literally the top coder in my branch, but socially I am completely invisible and it makes me want to drop out.

I'm scrolling through LinkedIn and Instagram and everyone's posting photos of their 'day out with the core team' or their placement parties. My roommate got a 24 LPA package and he's out celebrating with his group, and I'm sitting here on my bunk bed with a half-eaten packet of Maggi, realizing my phone hasn't pinged with a personal message in three days. I worked so hard to get into this college, but it feels like everyone else got a manual on how to make friends and live life, and my copy got lost in transition.

During the day, I can distract myself with lectures and assignments. But when it's 2 AM in the hostel, and I can hear the guys in the next room laughing, sharing jokes, and planning their weekend trip, the silence in my room becomes physically painful. They didn't even ask me if I wanted to join, even though I helped one of them pass his end-sem backlog last week. I feel like a utility to people—someone they use when they need notes, but completely discard when it's time to actually live.

Today is my 20th birthday. Back home, my mom would make kheer and we’d have a small family dinner. Here, my phone only rang once—it was an automated spam call from my bank wishing me. I sat in the library till 10 PM hoping someone from my lab group would at least post a quick 'HBD' on the WhatsApp group, but the chat stayed dead. I’m spending my birthday night debugging a broken compiler error because if I stop coding, the absolute emptiness of this place will crush me.

It happened again today in the DSA coding lab. The professor said 'form groups of three for the semester project' and my chest just went tight. Within thirty seconds, everyone was laughing, high-fiving, and pulling chairs together. I just sat there staring at my cursor, pretending to debug a loop that was already working. I ended up being the leftover person assigned to a random group of guys who didn't even look at me when I sat down. It's my second year here and I still feel like a ghost in my own department.

Every Friday night, the hostel mess empties out. People are either heading home or going out in big groups to the local cafes, shouting down the corridors. I sat at a long steel table tonight with just my plate of cold roti and dal, listening to the echoes of their laughter fade down the stairs. I tried scrolling Instagram to block it out, but seeing everyone's stories of house parties and late-night drives just made the silence in my room feel louder. I don't get what I'm doing wrong; I talk to people in lectures, but it never translates to actually being wanted.

Placement drive started this week, and the WhatsApp group is just a constant stream of congratulations for 15+ LPA packages. My dad called me today asking why my name isn't on the list yet, reminding me of how much they spent on my hostel fees. I have two backlogs I'm still trying to clear, and I can't even get past the first round of coding tests. I don't feel like I belong in this league of achievers; I'm just a disappointment taking up space in a room full of geniuses.

I moved to this city from a small town, and everyone in my wing speaks the local language so fast. When I walk down the hostel corridor, they all laugh at some inside joke, but the second I walk past, the conversation just dies down. I try to smile, but it feels so forced, like I'm an actor trying to audition for a play where I don't even know the script. I ended up staying in my room with the door locked all Sunday, pretending to study for a quiz just so I wouldn't have to face the awkwardness of not belonging.

It was my roommate's birthday last night, and they had this huge cake-cutting ceremony in the common room. I was there, standing at the very edge of the crowd, watching everyone smear cake on his face and take selfies. Someone handed me a piece of cake on a tissue paper without even looking at me, and I just realized... if I didn't show up, literally nobody would have noticed my absence. I went back to my bunk bed, turned my face to the wall, and cried quietly so nobody would hear me while the music was still blasting outside.

Every single night is the same. I walk into the hostel mess for dinner, and my stomach just knots up. Everyone is sitting in these tight, laughing groups talking about their DSA labs or who got shortlisted for the Microsoft internship, and I'm just standing there with my tray, looking for an empty corner so I don't have to awkwardly ask to sit next to someone who clearly doesn't want me there. I’ve been here for a whole semester and I still feel like a complete ghost walking through these corridors.

We had to form groups of four for the DBMS capstone project today. The professor said 'find your partners' and within two seconds, the entire lab was buzzing, people shouting across tables, and I just sat there staring at my VS Code screen, pretending to debug a script so I wouldn't look desperate. I ended up being assigned to a leftover group with two guys who already had backlogs and don't care, and they didn't even add me to their WhatsApp group chat. I feel like an absolute misfit who's just taking up space in this department.

It's Saturday night in the hostel, and the silence in my room is deafening. I just opened Instagram and saw the stories of my wingmates who all went to this cafe in town without even mentioning it in our wing group, even though we were just talking about midterms together yesterday. I’m sitting here with half-finished web-dev assignments, feeling this physical ache in my chest because I realized I'm only good for borrowing lab manuals, never for actually hanging out.

I moved from my hometown to this college across the country, and I feel like an alien. In the hostel block, everyone groups up by their state and speaks in their regional language, laughing at inside jokes I don't understand. I tried joining them during tea time, but the conversation kept drifting back to their native tongue, and I just stood there smiling like an idiot until I walked away. My CGPA is slipping because I can't even focus, just thinking about how I don't belong in this state, this college, or this life.

Placement season has started, and my WhatsApp is flooded with 'Congratulate XYZ for getting placed at Amazon' messages with salary packages that my parents keep sending me screenshots of. I haven't even cleared the first round of any coding test, and when I walk down the placement cell corridor, everyone is wearing formals and talking about their CTCs while I feel like a complete imposter who shouldn't even be in engineering. I have no friends to vent to, because everyone is competing with everyone else, and the sheer loneliness of this cutthroat race is suffocating me.

Everyone already has their lab groups sorted for the Operating Systems project. I stood there near the lab assistant's desk for ten minutes while everyone paired up, and no one even looked at me. I ended up getting assigned to a random group with two guys who don't even talk to me in the WhatsApp group; they just discuss everything on their personal chat. I sit in my hostel room staring at my DSA sheet, hearing the guys next door laugh and order pizza, and I just feel like a ghost who is completely invisible here.

It's the weekend and the entire wing of my hostel is completely empty because everyone went home or out on a trip together. I couldn't go because of my backlogs, so I'm just sitting here in the dim light of my room staring at the fan. I scrolled Instagram and saw my school friends posting pictures from their college fests, looking so happy and close with their new groups, while I can't even get someone to sit with me at the mess during dinner. I feel like there's some secret handbook on how to make friends that everyone else got at orientation, and I somehow missed it.

My parents kept telling everyone in our colony that I got into a premier college and that I'd be thriving, but the truth is I hate it here. During the mess introductions, my voice was shaking so bad because I didn't know the regional language, and everyone just chuckled. Now, whenever I walk down the corridor, I keep my eyes glued to my phone, pretending to be busy on WhatsApp so I don't have to face the awkwardness of nodding to people who don't even care if I exist. I feel like a massive disappointment to my family and a total outsider to my peers.

I survived the placement season and actually got a decent package, but looking at the group chat with all the congratulatory messages, I realized I have no one to actually celebrate with. Everyone else is planning celebratory dinners with their close circles, and I'm just sitting on my bed eating cold Maggie alone. My parents are thrilled on the phone, but once I hang up, the silence in this room is deafening. I spent four years grinding for a resume, but I forgot to build a life, and now I feel completely hollow and disconnected from everyone.

There is this group of people from my department who always sit in the campus canteen together, and they seem so warm and welcoming. Today, I finally gathered the courage to walk up and ask if I could sit with them because the other tables were full, but they just sort of shifted cold glances and said they were waiting for someone else. I walked away so fast my ears were burning, and I ended up skipping lunch entirely to hide in the library restroom. I just feel so fundamentally unlikable, like there is a giant warning sign on me that only other people can see.

I've been here for two semesters now and I still don't have a single person I can call to grab a maggi with. I feel like an NPC in everyone else's college life, just taking up physical space without actually existing.

I heard one of them sigh when the professor said my name. I just want to pack my bags, take a train back home, and never come back to this godforsaken engineering college.

My dad kept asking why my CGPA is a 6.8 and why I haven't cracked any hackathons like our neighbor's son who got a 20 LPA package. I couldn't even tell him that I spend my weekends locked in my hostel room because the guys in my wing speak a regional language I don't know and they never invite me to eat. I feel completely disconnected from my home, and like a total alien at my college.

I tried going to the college cultural fest today, thinking maybe if I just got out of my room I’d feel normal. Instead, I just stood in the crowd watching groups of friends take selfies, laugh at inside jokes, and hold hands. I ended up hiding in a bathroom stall for thirty minutes just to breathe before running back to my dorm. Scrolling through the fest stories on Instagram right now makes me feel like my chest is physically hollow.

Everyone in my branch has these tight-knit friend circles already, and when I try to sit next to them in the lecture hall, their conversations just carry on over my head like I'm made of glass. During lunch, I literally walk to the farthest mess on campus just so I don't have to sit alone in the main dining hall where everyone can see me. I'm so tired of pretending I'm reading an important email on my phone just to look like I have a life.

It's Friday night in the hostel, and my entire wing is out celebrating some guy's placement offer at a microbrewery. I'm sitting here in my room, staring at my DSA coding labs sheet and a half-eaten plate of maggi. I've tried so hard to fit in with these guys, but whenever they start talking in their regional language, I just freeze and pretend to look at my phone. It’s like I'm a ghost walking through these corridors; nobody would even notice if I didn't show up to the mess tomorrow.

We had to form groups of four for the DBMS mini-project today. The professor said 'find your partners' and within thirty seconds, the entire lab was buzzing, chairs scraping, people laughing. I just sat there, staring at my screen, pretending to debug a SQL query that was already working, waiting for the leftover group to claim me. I hate this place so much; it feels like high school all over again where I'm always the last option nobody actually wants.

My parents keeps sending me screenshots of my cousin’s LinkedIn updates about his new 18 LPA package at Amazon, asking why I haven't landed an internship yet. I scroll through Instagram and see my batchmates posting stories from their weekend trip to Gokarna, looking so effortless and happy. I’ve spent the last six weekends locked in my room preparing for interviews, but I feel totally disconnected from everyone here, like I’m running a race in the dark and nobody is waiting for me at the finish line.

I’m sitting in the corner of the hostel mess right now during dinner, and the noise is deafening—everyone is planning their trips for the upcoming vacation break. I’m just staring at my cold chapatis, trying to swallow the lump in my throat because my ticket home got cancelled due to the rail strike, and I have to stay back in an empty hostel wing alone. No one has even asked me if I want to join their plans; I am completely invisible in a room of three hundred people.

It's my birthday today. I was hoping someone from my project group or my wing would at least drop a text, but my phone has been dead silent all day except for the automated templates from my bank and college portal. I even went to the late-night canteen just to be around people, hoping someone would spot me and say something, but they were all engrossed in their own group chats. I ended up buying a single dairy milk silk, came back to my desk, and just cried while staring at my backlog syllabus.

It's DSA coding lab day and the professor asked us to form groups of three. Everyone instantly turned to their friends, high-fiving and grabbing seats together, while I just stood there pretending to fix my laptop charger so no one would see my hands shaking. I ended up being assigned to a group that already had three people, and they literally haven't looked at me or asked for my GitHub username once; they're just talking in their regional language and laughing. I feel like a complete ghost in this lab, like if I just packed my bag and walked out, they wouldn't even notice my seat was empty.

I've been in this college for four months now, and I still sit alone in the mess during dinner every single night. I scroll through Instagram on my phone pretend-texting people so I don't look like a total loser, while the table next to me is screaming, planning their weekend trip, and sharing food from their home towns. My mom called me yesterday asking if I made friends yet and I lied and said yeah, a bunch of us go out for tea after class. I hung up the phone and just stared at my hostel room wall, feeling this heavy, hollow ache in my chest that tells me I simply don't fit in here.

The placement cell just posted the spreadsheet of students placed in the dream companies on our official WhatsApp group, and the group chat is exploding with congrats messages and inside jokes. I'm sitting here with zero offers, two active backlogs, and a CGPA that won't even let me clear the eligibility criteria for the next round of companies. Watching my batchmates tag each other and celebrate makes me feel like I'm standing behind a thick glass wall, watching a life I'll never be allowed to join. I'm so far behind that I feel like an imposter even walking down the department corridor.

Every Friday evening, the entire wing of my hostel empties out as people head back to their nearby hometowns or go out to cafes in groups. The silence in the corridor is deafening, and the only sound is my own ceiling fan creaking at speed three. I tried joining the literary club and the coding club, but during meetings, everyone already has their pre-established cliques and I just end up sitting in the back row, nodding along like an idiot. I'm starting to think there is something fundamentally broken in me that keeps me from connecting with anyone on more than a superficial level.

My wingmates are all from the southern states and they constantly speak in their regional language, laughing at memes and sharing inside jokes from back home. I'm the only North Indian on this floor, and whenever I enter the common room, the conversation either awkwardly dies down or someone has to reluctantly translate for me. I hate being the burden that ruins their flow, so now I just lock myself in my room from 6 PM onwards, pretending I'm grinding on LeetCode. I'm sick of feeling like an alien in my own living space, eating instant noodles alone because going to the mess feels like walking into a trial where I don't speak the language.

It’s 8:30 PM and I'm sitting at the corner table of the hostel mess, staring at my plate of cold dal. Everyone around me is sitting in these loud, laughing groups talking about their DSA coding labs and some coding test they all cracked. They speak in this regional language I barely understand, and every time I try to catch someone’s eye, they just look right through me. I spent my entire afternoon trying to fix a bug in my project alone, and now I’m eating alone. I feel like an absolute ghost on this campus, like if I packed my bags and left tonight, not a single soul would even notice my empty bed.

We had to form groups of four for our DBMS capstone project today, and it was my absolute nightmare. Within two minutes, everyone was high-fiving, pulling chairs together, and forming their teams while I just sat there pretending to scroll through my phone so I wouldn't look pathetic. The professor literally had to announce, 'Is there anyone left?' and then forced me into a group that clearly didn't want a fifth member. I could see the micro-expressions of disappointment on their faces, and they didn't even add me to their WhatsApp group chat. I’m sitting in my dorm room right now, crying because I feel so incredibly unwanted and out of place.

It's Saturday night and the hostel corridor is dead silent because literally everyone went out to celebrate Rohan’s 12 LPA placement package. I’m stuck here in my dark room with a pile of backlogs and a 6.2 CGPA, scrolling through Instagram and seeing their stories of them raising glasses and taking group selfies. It’s not even just about the job; it’s that they have this tight-knit brotherhood where they share everything, and I’m just the weird guy next door who only gets asked for a phone charger. I feel this massive, hollow ache in my chest, like I’m some defective piece of machinery that doesn't belong in this ecosystem.

Yesterday was my 20th birthday. I spent months contributing to everyone else's cake funds, midnight birthday bumps, and group gifts in our wing. But last night? Absolutely nothing happened. A couple of dry 'HBD' texts on the wing group chat, but no one knocked on my door, no one brought a 10-rupee dairy milk, nothing. I sat in the dark listening to the guys in the next room screaming while playing FIFA. It made me realize that all these 'friendships' I thought I was building are completely superficial; I am just a filler character in their lives while they are main characters in mine.

The college cultural fest is happening right now, and the entire campus is buzzing with energy, music, and colorful lights. I dressed up and went down to the main arena, but within ten minutes, the sheer volume of tight cliques, couples holding hands, and inside jokes made me feel dizzy. I was just wandering around like an NPC, pretending to search for someone on my phone so I didn't look completely friendless. I ended up walking back to my room, locking the door, and pulling the bedsheet over my head. Why is it that the more people there are around me, the more brutally alone I feel?

Everyone in the wing already has their groups. During the DSA labs, when the prof says 'form teams of three,' my stomach just drops. I stand there pretending to check my phone while everyone immediately pairs up and laughs. I ended up being assigned to a random group of guys who didn't even talk to me; they just did the code on Github and submitted it. I'm in my second year, my CGPA is slipping to 6.8, and I feel like an absolute ghost in this hostel.

I don't speak the local language here, and every evening the corridor erupts into these fast-paced conversations in Telugu. I tried sitting with them in the mess hall once, but within five minutes, they switched back from English and I was just staring at my plate of cold rice, nodding like an idiot. Now I just skip dinner or order rolls to my room so I don't have to face that awkward silence. My parents keep asking over WhatsApp if I've made friends, and I just send them emojis because telling them I'm completely alone would break their hearts.

The placement announcements started this week. The WhatsApp group is flooded with 'Congratulations to my brother for getting placed at Microsoft!' with hundreds of thumbs-up emojis. I have three backlogs in math, I haven't even touched my resume, and I spent the entire weekend just staring at the fan in my room while my roommate was out celebrating his 14 LPA package. I feel like this college is a fast-moving train and I've been thrown off on the tracks, forgotten and useless.

It's Diwali weekend and almost the entire hostel has vacated to go home. I couldn't go because ticket prices spiked and my family couldn't afford it this time. Walking down the empty, dark corridors is actually terrifying—it's like a ghost town. I can hear the distant sound of crackers outside, and I've just been scrolling Instagram watching everyone's stories of family pujas and heavy sweets while eating a dry packet of Maggi in my room. I've never felt this invisible in my entire life.

I joined the college music club thinking I'd finally find 'my people.' But even there, it feels like high school all over again. The seniors only jam with their old friend circle, and the other freshmen are so loud and confident, talking about their cool high school bands. I just sat in the corner of the music room holding my guitar, too scared to even tune it. I left early during the jam session, and nobody even noticed I walked out of the door.

It happened again in the DBMS lab today. The professor said, 'Form teams of three for the term project,' and within ten seconds, everyone was high-fiving, pulling chairs together, and laughing. I just sat there, staring at my empty VS Code terminal, pretending I was busy writing some queries so nobody would see how pathetic I looked. Eventually, the TA had to manually assign me to a random group of guys who already looked annoyed that they had to 'carry' me. I've been in this hostel for six months and I still feel like a piece of furniture that got delivered to the wrong address.

Friday nights are the absolute worst in this hostel. The whole wing gets quiet because everyone goes out in their little groups to the local cafes, or they are huddled in the corner rooms speaking in their regional language, laughing at inside jokes I can't understand. I just sit on my squeaky metal bed, staring at my pending DSA backlog, listening to the hum of the corridor. I tried joining them in the common room last week, but I just stood there on the edge of the circle like some weird NPC. I don’t think anyone would even notice if I packed my bags and went home tonight.

My entire WhatsApp feed is just placement screenshots of people getting 15+ LPA packages at tech giants, and my family keeps calling me asking when I'm going to land a referral. In the mess hall, all anyone talks about is system design, competitive coding, and mock interviews. I sat at a table today and tried to change the subject to literally anything else—even a movie—and there was this dead silence before someone said, 'Well, movies don't pay the bills,' and went back to discussing LeetCode. I feel like a total alien here; I don't care about their hustle culture, but staying away makes me feel completely abandoned and alone.

Yesterday was my 20th birthday and literally not a single person in this building noticed. I spent the evening scrolling through Instagram, watching stories of people from my department getting their faces smeared with cake in the hostel courtyard while everyone sang for them. I even left my door slightly ajar hoping someone from my wing would just pop their head in and say 'happy birthday,' but people just walked right past to go to the washroom. It's ridiculous how much it hurt to blow out a single candle on a bakery cupcake I bought for myself.

We were sitting on the hostel terrace last night at 2 AM, and everyone was sharing these deep, sentimental stories about their school days and childhood friends. I finally gathered the courage to share how much I struggle with anxiety and how lonely my first year of college has been, expecting some kind of comfort. Instead, the guy next to me just laughed it off and said, 'Bro, wait till you see the end-sem paper, then you'll know real anxiety,' and everyone shifted the topic back to exam tips. I felt this instant, cold wave of shame wash over me; I opened my chest up to them, and they just stepped over it.

It happened again in the DSA lab today. The prof said 'form groups of three' and my heart just dropped to my stomach. Everyone immediately looked at each other, high-fived, and paired up within five seconds. I stood there clutching my keyboard, pretending to debug a segment fault just to look busy. The TA eventually forced me into a group of two who already looked annoyed that they had to 'carry' me. I’m in my third semester, my CGPA is a 6.8, and I feel like an absolute ghost walking through this campus. Does anyone else feel like they're just background noise in everyone else's college life?

I dread 8:30 PM every single night. Walking into the hostel mess is like running a gauntlet of inside jokes and loud laughter that I have no part of. I grab my plate of cold rotis, look around at all the packed tables where people are shouting over each other about placement offers, and end up sitting at the corner-most broken table facing the wall. I eat as fast as I can, keeping my eyes glued to my phone, pretending I'm reading an important email when really my hands are shaking. I’m surrounded by five hundred people in this hostel but I have never felt more utterly, devastatingly alone.

I came halfway across the country for this engineering degree, but everyone here already has their pre-established regional cliques. The moment I sit down at the corridor, the conversation flips from English to a local language I don't speak a word of, and they all laugh at a joke I'll never understand. I try to smile and nod along, but I feel like a complete imposter, a piece of cardboard leaning against the wall. When I go back to my empty room, I just stare at the ceiling and wonder if I made the biggest mistake of my life leaving my hometown.

My WhatsApp group is blowing up with congratulations. Everyone is posting their double-tick green status updates about landing 15 LPA packages at major tech firms, while I’m sitting here with three backlogs in coding papers and a blank resume. During the department group photo today, I literally stood at the very edge of the back row, hoping the photographer would just crop me out because I don't belong in their success story. My dad keeps calling to ask if the placement drive has started for me, and I just disconnect the call because the shame of being the class failure is eating me alive.

It's Diwali weekend and literally the entire hostel has cleared out. I couldn't afford the flight ticket back home, so I'm the only soul left on the third floor. Walking down the dark corridor to get water is terrifyingly silent—no doors opening, no loud music, just the echo of my own slippers. I scrolled through Instagram and saw everyone posing with their families in ethnic clothes, or setting off crackers in their backyards, while I'm eating instant noodles in a room that smells like dust and damp laundry. I feel like if I disappeared from this dorm tonight, nobody would even notice until the next semester starts.
